sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 2nd April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Let $|A|=0\Rightarrow αβ-(-6)=0\Rightarrow αβ=-6$ and $α+β=1\Rightarrow α,β$ are roots of the equation

$\begin{array}{lllll} x^{2}-x-6=0\Rightarrow x=3,-2.\text{Since}α>0 \\ \Rightarrow α=3,β=-2 \\ \Rightarrow A=\left [\begin{array}{ll} 3 & -1 \\ 6 & -2 \end{array}\right ]\Rightarrow I+A=\left [\begin{array}{ll} 4 & -1 \\ 6 & -1 \end{array}\right ] \\ (I+A)^{2}=\left [\begin{array}{ll} 10 & -3 \\ 18 & -5 \end{array}\right ]\Rightarrow (I+A)^{4}=\left [\begin{array}{ll} 46 & -15 \\ 90 & -29 \end{array}\right ] \\ \Rightarrow (I+A)^{8}=\left [\begin{array}{ll} 766 & -255 \\ 1530 & -509 \end{array}\right ] \end{array}$

text: Let $a\in R$ and $A$ be a matrix of order $3\times 3$ such that $\det (A)=-4$ and $A+I=\left [\begin{array}{lll} 1 & a & 1 \\ 2 & 1 & 0 \\ a & 1 & 2 \end{array}\right ]$, where $I$ is the identity matrix of order $3\times 3$. If $\det ((a+1)\mathrm{adj}((a-1)A))$ is $2^{\mathrm{m}}3^{\mathrm{n}},\mathrm{m}$, $\mathrm{n}\in \{0,1,2,\ldots ,20\}$, then $\mathrm{m}+\mathrm{n}$ is equal to :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 2nd April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Given

$A+I=\left [\begin{array}{lll} 1 & a & 1 \\ 2 & 1 & 0 \\ a & 1 & 2 \end{array}\right ]$

So,

$A=\left [\begin{array}{lll} 1-1 & a & 1 \\ 2 & 1-1 & 0 \\ a & 1 & 2-1 \end{array}\right ]=\left [\begin{array}{lll} 0 & a & 1 \\ 2 & 0 & 0 \\ a & 1 & 1 \end{array}\right ]$

1) Find $a$ using $\det (A)=-4$
Compute $\det (A)$ by expanding along the first row:

$\det (A)=0\cdot C_{11}+a\cdot C_{12}+1\cdot C_{13}$

Now,

$C_{12}=(-1)^{1+2}\left |\begin{array}{ll} 2 & 0 \\ a & 1 \end{array}\right |=-(2\cdot 1-0\cdot a)=-2$

$C_{13}=(-1)^{1+3}\left |\begin{array}{ll} 2 & 0 \\ a & 1 \end{array}\right |=+(2\cdot 1-0\cdot a)=2$

So,

$\det (A)=a(-2)+1(2)=2-2a=2(1-a)$

Given $\det (A)=-4$:

$2(1-a)=-4⟹1-a=-2⟹a=3$

2) Evaluate $\det ((a+1)\mathrm{adj}((a-1)A))$
Use properties for a $3\times 3$ matrix:

$\det (kM)=k^{3}\det (M)$

$\det (\mathrm{adj}(M))=(\det M)^{3-1}=(\det M)^{2}$

$\det ((a-1)A)=(a-1)^{3}\det (A)$

Let $B=(a-1)A$. Then

$\det ((a+1)\mathrm{adj}(B))=(a+1)^{3}\det (\mathrm{adj}(B))=(a+1)^{3}(\det B)^{2}$

Now,

$\det B=((a-1)^{3})(\det A)=(a-1)^{3}(-4)$

So,

$\det ((a+1)\mathrm{adj}((a-1)A))=(a+1)^{3}\left [(-4)(a-1)^{3}\right ]^{2}=(a+1)^{3}\cdot 16\cdot (a-1)^{6}$

Put $a=3$:

$(a+1)^{3}=4^{3}=2^{6},(a-1)^{6}=2^{6},16=2^{4}$

Hence,

$\text{Determinant}=2^{6}\cdot 2^{4}\cdot 2^{6}=2^{16}=2^{m}3^{n}$

So $m=16,n=0⟹m+n=16$.

Answer: 16 (Option D)
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2025 (Online) 2nd April Morning Shift

text: If $S$ and $S^{'}$ are the foci of the ellipse $\frac{x^{2}}{18}+\frac{y^{2}}{9}=1$ and P be a point on the ellipse, then $\min (SP\cdot S^{'}P)+\max (SP\cdot S^{'}P)$ is equal to :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 2nd April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Here $a^{2}=18$ and $b^{2}=9$, so $a=3\sqrt{2}$ and $e=\sqrt{1-\dfrac{9}{18}}=\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$; the foci are $S(3,0)$ and $S^{'}(-3,0)$.


[IMG]

For $P(x,y)$ on the ellipse the focal distances are $SP=a-ex$ and $S^{'}P=a+ex$ (so $SP+S^{'}P=2a$), hence

$SP\cdot S^{'}P=a^{2}-e^{2}x^{2}=18-\dfrac{x^{2}}{2},-3\sqrt{2}\leq x\leq 3\sqrt{2}$

The maximum is at $x=0$ (ends of the minor axis): $18$.

The minimum is at $x^{2}=18$ (ends of the major axis): $18-9=9$.

$\min (SP\cdot S^{'}P)+\max (SP\cdot S^{'}P)=9+18=27$

Hence, the correct option is (C).

text: Let the focal chord PQ of the parabola $y^{2}=4x$ make an angle of $60^{\circ }$ with the positive $x$ axis, where P lies in the first quadrant. If the circle, whose one diameter is PS, S being the focus of the parabola, touches the $y$-axis at the point $(0,α)$, then $5α^{2}$ is equal to:
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 2nd April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
For $y^{2}=4x$, $a=1$ and the focus is $S(1,0)$. Let $P(t^{2},2t)$ with $t>0$, since $P$ is in the first quadrant.

The focal chord makes $60^{\circ }$ with the positive $x$-axis, so the slope of $PS$ is $\sqrt{3}$:

$\dfrac{2t}{t^{2}-1}=\sqrt{3}\Rightarrow \sqrt{3}t^{2}-2t-\sqrt{3}=0\Rightarrow (t-\sqrt{3})(\sqrt{3}t+1)=0$

With $t>0$, $t=\sqrt{3}$ and $P(3,2\sqrt{3})$.

The circle with diameter $PS$ has centre $\left (\dfrac{3+1}{2},\dfrac{2\sqrt{3}+0}{2}\right )=(2,\sqrt{3})$ and radius $\dfrac{PS}{2}=\dfrac{1+3}{2}=2$, since the focal distance $PS=1+t^{2}=4$.

The distance of the centre from the $y$-axis is $2$, equal to the radius, so the circle touches the $y$-axis at the foot of the perpendicular from the centre, $(0,\sqrt{3})$.

So $α=\sqrt{3}$ and $5α^{2}=15$.

Hence, the correct option is (A).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2025 (Online) 2nd April Morning Shift

text: If the function $f(x)=2x^{3}-9ax^{2}+12\mathrm{a}^{2}x+1$, where $\mathrm{a}>0$, attains its local maximum and local minimum values at p and q , respectively, such that $\mathrm{p}^{2}=\mathrm{q}$, then $f(3)$ is equal to :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 2nd April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
To determine the value of $f(3)$ for the function $f(x)=2x^{3}-9ax^{2}+12a^{2}x+1$, where $a>0$, we follow these steps:

First, find the critical points by setting the derivative equal to zero:

$f^{'}(x)=6x^{2}-18ax+12a^{2}=0$

Factoring gives:

$6(x-a)(x-2a)=0$

Thus, the critical points are $x=a$ and $x=2a$.

$x=a$ corresponds to a local maximum.

$x=2a$ corresponds to a local minimum.

According to the problem, $p^{2}=q$. Substituting $p=a$ and $q=2a$ gives:

$a^{2}=2a$

Solving for $a$ gives:

$a(a-2)=0$

Since $a>0$, we have $a=2$.

Now, substitute $a=2$ back into the function:

$f(x)=2x^{3}-18x^{2}+48x+1$

To find $f(3)$:

$f(3)=2(3)^{3}-18(3)^{2}+48(3)+1$

Calculate each term:

$2(3)^{3}=54$

$18(3)^{2}=162$

$48(3)=144$

Thus, 

$f(3)=54-162+144+1=37$

So, $f(3)=37$.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2025 (Online) 2nd April Morning Shift

text: Let one focus of the hyperbola $\mathrm{H}:\frac{x^{2}}{\mathrm{a}^{2}}-\frac{y^{2}}{\mathrm{b}^{2}}=1$ be at $(\sqrt{10},0)$ and the corresponding directrix be $x=\frac{9}{\sqrt{10}}$. If $e$ and $l$ respectively are the eccentricity and the length of the latus rectum of H , then $9\left (e^{2}+l\right )$ is equal to :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 2nd April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\frac{x^{2}}{a^{2}}-\frac{y^{2}}{b^{2}}=1$

Directrix : $x=\frac{9}{\sqrt{10}}=\frac{a}{e}\text{..... (i)}$

Focus : $(\sqrt{10},0)\equiv (ae,0)$

$ae=\sqrt{10}\text{..... (ii)}$

(i) $\times$ (ii)

$\Rightarrow a^{2}=9\Rightarrow a=3$

Substitute in (ii)

$e=\frac{\sqrt{10}}{3}$

$\begin{array}{l} \text{Now}e^{2}=1+\dfrac{b^{2}}{a^{2}} \\ \dfrac{10}{9}=1+\dfrac{b^{2}}{a} \\ \Rightarrow b=1 \\ I=\dfrac{2b^{2}}{a}=\dfrac{2\times 1}{3}=\dfrac{2}{3} \\ a\left [e^{2}+l\right ]=9\left [\dfrac{10}{9}+\dfrac{2}{3}\right ]=10+6 \\ =16 \end{array}$

text: Let $\mathrm{P}_{\mathrm{n}}=α^{\mathrm{n}}+β^{\mathrm{n}},\mathrm{n}\in \mathrm{N}$. If $\mathrm{P}_{10}=123,\mathrm{P}_{9}=76,\mathrm{P}_{8}=47$ and $\mathrm{P}_{1}=1$, then the quadratic equation having roots $\frac{1}{α}$ and $\frac{1}{β}$ is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 2nd April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Given

$P_{n}=α^{n}+β^{n}$

and

$P_{10}=123,P_{9}=76,P_{8}=47,P_{1}=1.$

We want the quadratic equation whose roots are $\dfrac{1}{α}$ and $\dfrac{1}{β}$.

For numbers $α,β$, the sequence $P_{n}=α^{n}+β^{n}$ satisfies

$P_{n}=(α+β)P_{n-1}-(αβ)P_{n-2}.$

Now use the given values:

$P_{10}=(α+β)P_{9}-(αβ)P_{8}.$

So,

$123=(α+β)\cdot 76-(αβ)\cdot 47.$

Also, since $P_{1}=α+β=1$, we get

$123=76-47αβ.$

Thus,

$47=-47αβ,$

so

$αβ=-1.$

Now the roots needed are $\dfrac{1}{α}$ and $\dfrac{1}{β}$.

Their sum is

$\frac{1}{α}+\frac{1}{β}=\frac{α+β}{αβ}=\frac{1}{-1}=-1.$

Their product is

$\frac{1}{αβ}=\frac{1}{-1}=-1.$

A quadratic equation with roots $r_{1},r_{2}$ is

$x^{2}-(r_{1}+r_{2})x+r_{1}r_{2}=0.$

Here,

$x^{2}-(-1)x+(-1)=0,$

which gives

$x^{2}+x-1=0.$

So the correct option is:

$x^{2}+x-1=0$

Option A.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2025 (Online) 2nd April Morning Shift

text: If $\vec{\mathrm{a}}$ is a nonzero vector such that its projections on the vectors $2\hat{i}-\hat{j}+2\hat{k},\hat{i}+2\hat{j}-2\hat{k}$ and $\hat{k}$ are equal, then a unit vector along $\vec{\mathrm{a}}$ is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 2nd April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The projection of $⃗{a}$ on $⃗{v}$ is $\dfrac{⃗{a}\cdot ⃗{v}}{|⃗{v}|}$. Here $|2\hat{i}-\hat{j}+2\hat{k}|=|\hat{i}+2\hat{j}-2\hat{k}|=3$ and $|\hat{k}|=1$.

With $⃗{a}=x\hat{i}+y\hat{j}+z\hat{k}$, equal projections give

$\dfrac{2x-y+2z}{3}=z=\dfrac{x+2y-2z}{3}$

The first equality gives $2x-y+2z=3z$, so $y=2x-z$. The second gives $x+2y-2z=3z$, so $x+2y=5z$.

Substituting: $x+4x-2z=5z\Rightarrow x=\dfrac{7z}{5}$, and then $y=\dfrac{14z}{5}-z=\dfrac{9z}{5}$.

So $⃗{a}=\dfrac{z}{5}(7\hat{i}+9\hat{j}+5\hat{k})$ with $z\neq 0$; for $7\hat{i}+9\hat{j}+5\hat{k}$ each projection equals 5.

Since $|7\hat{i}+9\hat{j}+5\hat{k}|=\sqrt{49+81+25}=\sqrt{155}$, a unit vector along $⃗{a}$ is $\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{155}}(7\hat{i}+9\hat{j}+5\hat{k})$ (the opposite unit vector is not among the options).

Hence, the correct option is (D).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2025 (Online) 2nd April Morning Shift

text:
If the system of linear equations

$\begin{array}{l} 3x+y+βz=3 \\ 2x+αy-z=-3 \\ x+2y+z=4 \end{array}$

has infinitely many solutions, then the value of $22β-9α$ is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 2nd April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\begin{array}{lllllllllllllllllll} \begin{array}{l} 3x+y+βz=3 \\ 2x+αy-z=-3 \\ x+2y+z=4 \end{array} \\ \text{has infinite solution} \\ \begin{array}{lllllll} \Rightarrow \Delta =0,\Delta _{1}=\Delta _{2}=\Delta _{3}=0 \\ \Delta =0\Rightarrow \left |\begin{array}{lll} 3 & 1 & β \\ 2 & α & -1 \\ 1 & 2 & 1 \end{array}\right |=0 \\ \Delta _{2}=0\Rightarrow \left |\begin{array}{lll} 3 & 3 & β \\ 2 & -3 & -1 \\ 1 & 4 & 1 \end{array}\right |=0 \\ \Rightarrow 3(-3+4)-3(2+1)+β(8+3)=0 \\ \Rightarrow 3-9+11β=0 \\ \Rightarrow β=\dfrac{6}{11} \\ \Delta _{3}=0\Rightarrow \left |\begin{array}{lll} 3 & 1 & 3 \\ 2 & α & -3 \\ 1 & 2 & 4 \end{array}\right |=0 \\ \Rightarrow 3(4α+6)-1(8+3)+3(4-α)=0 \\ 12α+18-11+12-3α=0 \\ 9α=-19 \\ α=\dfrac{-19}{9} \end{array} \end{array}$

$\therefore 22β-9α=31$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2025 (Online) 2nd April Morning Shift

text:
Let $f:𝐑\to 𝐑$ be a twice differentiable function such that $(\sin x\cos y)(f(2x+2y)-f(2x-2y))=(\cos x\sin y)(f(2x+2y)+f(2x-2y))$, for all $x,y\in 𝐑$.
If $f^{'}(0)=\frac{1}{2}$, then the value of $24f^{''}\left (\frac{5π}{3}\right )$ is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 2nd April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Collecting the terms in $f(2x+2y)$ and $f(2x-2y)$:

$f(2x+2y)(\sin x\cos y-\cos x\sin y)=f(2x-2y)(\sin x\cos y+\cos x\sin y)$

$f(2x+2y)\sin (x-y)=f(2x-2y)\sin (x+y)\Rightarrow \frac{f(2x+2y)}{\sin (x+y)}=\frac{f(2x-2y)}{\sin (x-y)}$

Since $x+y$ and $x-y$ take any values independently, both sides equal a constant $k$. So $f(2u)=k\sin u$ for all $u$, that is, $f(x)=k\sin \dfrac{x}{2}$.

$f^{'}(x)=\dfrac{k}{2}\cos \dfrac{x}{2}$, and $f^{'}(0)=\dfrac{k}{2}=\dfrac{1}{2}$ gives $k=1$.

$f^{''}(x)=-\dfrac{1}{4}\sin \dfrac{x}{2}$, so $f^{''}\left (\dfrac{5π}{3}\right )=-\dfrac{1}{4}\sin \dfrac{5π}{6}=-\dfrac{1}{4}\cdot \dfrac{1}{2}=-\dfrac{1}{8}$.

$24f^{''}\left (\frac{5π}{3}\right )=24\times \left (-\frac{1}{8}\right )=-3$

Hence, the correct option is (C).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2025 (Online) 2nd April Morning Shift

text: Let A be the set of all functions $f:𝐙\to 𝐙$ and R be a relation on A such that $\mathrm{R}=\{(\mathrm{f},\mathrm{g}):f(0)=\mathrm{g}(1)$ and $f(1)=\mathrm{g}(0)\}$. Then R is :
options: Symmetric and transitive but not reflexive
Symmetric but neither reflexive nor transitive
Transitive but neither reflexive nor symmetric
Reflexive but neither symmetric nor transitive
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 2nd April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$(f,f)\in R$ requires $f(0)=f(1)$. For $f(x)=x$, $f(0)=0\neq 1=f(1)$, so $(f,f)\notin R$ and R is not reflexive.

If $(f,g)\in R$, then $f(0)=g(1)$ and $f(1)=g(0)$, that is, $g(0)=f(1)$ and $g(1)=f(0)$, which is exactly the condition $(g,f)\in R$. So R is symmetric.

Take $f(x)=x$ and $g(x)=1-x$. Then $g(1)=0=f(0)$ and $g(0)=1=f(1)$, so $(f,g)\in R$, and by symmetry $(g,f)\in R$. Transitivity would then force $(f,f)\in R$, which is false. So R is not transitive.

Hence, the correct option is (B).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2025 (Online) 2nd April Morning Shift

text: The number of sequences of ten terms, whose terms are either 0 or 1 or 2 , that contain exactly five 1 s and exactly three 2 s , is equal to :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 2nd April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
To find the number of sequences of ten terms, each being either 0, 1, or 2, containing exactly five 1s and exactly three 2s, follow these steps:

Determine the Remaining Terms: Since there are 5 ones and 3 twos, you will need 2 zeros to fill the sequence (because $5+3+2=10$).

Calculate the Number of Arrangements: You have a total of 10 positions to fill with these numbers (5 ones, 3 twos, 2 zeros). The formula for calculating permutations of a multiset is:

$\frac{10!}{5!\times 3!\times 2!}$

Where:

$10!$ is the factorial of the total number of terms.

$5!$ is the factorial for the number of 1s.

$3!$ is the factorial for the number of 2s.

$2!$ is the factorial for the number of 0s.

Result: Simplifying the calculation gives:

$\frac{10!}{5!\times 3!\times 2!}=2520$

Thus, there are 2520 possible sequences with the given conditions.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2025 (Online) 2nd April Morning Shift

text: For $α,β,γ\in 𝐑$, if $\lim _{x\to 0}\frac{x^{2}\sin αx+(γ-1)\mathrm{e}^{x2}}{\sin 2x-βx}=3$, then $β+γ-α$ is equal to :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 2nd April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\begin{array}{l} \text{At}x\to 0 \\ \sin 2x-βx\to 0 \\ \Rightarrow \dfrac{0}{0}\text{form} \\ \Rightarrow (γ-1)e^{0}+0\sin (αx)\to 0 \\ \Rightarrow (γ-1)=0 \\ \Rightarrow γ=1 \\ \Rightarrow \lim _{x\to 0}\dfrac{x^{2}\sin (αx)}{(\sin 2x-βx)}=3 \end{array}$

$\Rightarrow \lim _{x\to 0}\frac{x^{2}\left [αx-\frac{(αx)3}{3!}+\frac{(αx)5}{5!}-\cdots \right ]}{\left [(2x)-\frac{(2x)3}{3!}+\frac{(2x)5}{5!}\right ]-βx}$

$\Rightarrow \lim _{x\to 0}\frac{αx^{3}-\frac{α3x5}{3!}+\frac{α5x7}{5!}-\cdots }{x(2-β)-\frac{8x3}{6}+\frac{2 5\cdot x5}{5!}-\cdots }=3$

$\begin{array}{ll} \Rightarrow  & 2-β=0\text{and}\dfrac{α}{\frac{-8}{6}}=3 \\ \Rightarrow  & β=2 \\ \quad α=3\left (-\dfrac{8}{6}\right )=-4 \\ \Rightarrow  & γ=1,β=2,α=-4 \\ \Rightarrow  & β+γ-α=7 \end{array}$

text: The term independent of $x$ in the expansion of $\left (\frac{(x+1)}{\left (x^{2/3}+1-x^{1/3}\right )}-\frac{(x-1)}{\left (x-x^{1/2}\right )}\right )^{10},x>1$, is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 2nd April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\left (\frac{x+1}{x^{2/3}-x^{1/3}+1}-\frac{x-1}{x-x^{1/2}}\right )^{10}$

= $\left (\frac{\left (x^{1/3}\right )^{3}+\left (1^{1/3}\right )^{3}}{x^{2/3}-x^{1/3}+1}-\frac{\left (\sqrt{x}\right )^{2}-(1)^{2}}{x-x^{1/2}}\right )^{10}$

= $\left (\frac{\left (x^{1/3}+1\right )\left (x^{2/3}-x^{1/3}+1\right )}{x^{2/3}-x^{1/3}+1}-\frac{\left (\sqrt{x}+1\right )\left (\sqrt{x}-1\right )}{\sqrt{x}\left (\sqrt{x}-1\right )}\right )^{10}$

= $\left (\left (x^{1/3}+1\right )-\frac{\left (\sqrt{x}+1\right )}{\sqrt{x}}\right )^{10}$

= $\left (\left (x^{1/3}+1\right )-\left (1+\frac{1}{\sqrt{x}}\right )\right )^{10}$

= $\left (x^{1/3}-\frac{1}{x^{1/2}}\right )^{10}$

[Note:

For $\left (x^{α}\pm \frac{1}{x^{β}}\right )^{n}$ the $(r+1)^{th}$ term with power m of x is 

$r=\frac{nα-m}{α+β}$]

Here $α=\frac{1}{3}$, $β=\frac{1}{2}$ and m = 0

then $r=\frac{10\times \frac{1}{3}-0}{\frac{1}{3}+\frac{1}{2}}$ = $\frac{10}{3}\times \frac{6}{5}$ = 4

$\therefore$ $T_{5}$ is the term independent of x.

$\therefore$ $T_{5} =$ ${}^{10}C_{4}$ = 210

text: Let $a_{1},a_{2},a_{3},\ldots$ be in an A.P. such that $\sum\limits _{k=1}^{12}a_{2k-1}=-\frac{72}{5}a_{1},a_{1}\neq 0$. If $\sum\limits _{k=1}^{n}a_{k}=0$, then $n$ is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 2nd April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Given:  

$\sum\limits _{k=1}^{12}a_{2k-1}=-\frac{72}{5}a_{1}$

This means:

$a_{1}+a_{3}+\cdots +a_{23}=-\frac{72}{5}a_{1}$

Express each term in A.P.:  

The general term of the A.P. is given by $a_{k}=a+(k-1)d$. Thus, for the odd indices:

$a_{1}+(a+2d)+(a+4d)+\cdots +(a+22d)$

Simplify the equation:  

$12a+2d(1+2+\cdots +11)=-\frac{72}{5}a$

Use the formula for sum of an arithmetic series (first 11 terms):  

$1+2+\cdots +11=\frac{11\times 12}{2}=66$

So, the equation becomes:

$12a+2d(66)=-\frac{72}{5}a$

$12a+132d=-\frac{72}{5}a$

Solve for the relationship between $a$ and $d$:  

$132d=-\frac{72}{5}a-12a$

$132d=-\frac{132}{5}a$

So, 

$a=-5d\text{(i)}$

Second condition:  

$\sum\limits _{k=1}^{n}a_{k}=0\Rightarrow S_{n}=0$

$\frac{n}{2}[2a+(n-1)d]=0$

$2a=-(n-1)d\text{(ii)}$

Combine equation (i) and (ii):  

Substitute $a=-5d$ into equation (ii):

$2(-5d)=-(n-1)d$

$-10d=-(n-1)d$

Therefore:

$n-1=10$

$n=11$

Thus, $n=11$.

text: Three distinct numbers are selected randomly from the set $\{1,2,3,\ldots ,40\}$. If the probability, that the selected numbers are in an increasing G.P., is $\frac{m}{n},\gcd (m,n)=1$, then $m+n$ is equal to $__________$ .
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 2nd April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Total selections: $\left (40 3\right )=9880$. Each favourable set is counted once, written in increasing order.

Three integers in increasing G.P. with ratio $r=\dfrac{p}{q}$, where $p>q\geq 1$ and $\gcd (p,q)=1$, have the form $kq^{2},kpq,kp^{2}$ with $k\in \mathrm{ℕ}$, since $a\cdot \dfrac{p^{2}}{q^{2}}$ is an integer only when $q^{2}$ divides $a$.

All three terms lie in $\{1,\ldots ,40\}$ exactly when $kp^{2}\leq 40$, so each coprime pair $(p,q)$ gives $⌊\dfrac{40}{p^{2}}⌋$ sets, and $p\leq 6$.

$p=2$ ($q=1$): $1\times 10=10$; $p=3$ ($q=1,2$): $2\times 4=8$; $p=4$ ($q=1,3$): $2\times 2=4$; $p=5$ ($q=1,2,3,4$): $4\times 1=4$; $p=6$ ($q=1,5$): $2\times 1=2$.

Favourable sets $=10+8+4+4+2=28$.

$P=\dfrac{28}{9880}=\dfrac{7}{2470}$

Since $2470=2\times 5\times 13\times 19$ has no factor 7, $m=7$, $n=2470$ and $m+n=2477$.

Hence, the answer is 2477.

text: Let $f:𝐑\to 𝐑$ be a thrice differentiable odd function satisfying $f^{'}(x)\geq 0,f^{''}(x)=f(x),f(0)=0,f^{'}(0)=3$. Then $9f(\log _{e}3)$ is equal to $__________$ .
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 2nd April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\begin{array}{l} f^{'}(x)\geq 0,f^{''}(x)=f(x) \\ \text{Second order differential equation} \end{array}$

$\begin{array}{l} f(x)=Ae^{x}+Be^{-x} \\ f(0)=0\Rightarrow A=-B \\ \Rightarrow f(x)=A\left (e^{x}-e^{-x}\right ) \\ f^{'}(x)=Ae^{x}+Ae^{-x}=A\left (e^{x}+e^{-x}\right ) \\ f^{'}(0)=3=A\left (e^{0}+e^{-0}\right )=2A\Rightarrow A=\dfrac{3}{2} \\ f(x)=\dfrac{3}{2}\left (e^{x}-e^{-x}\right ) \\ \text{If}(\ln 3)=\dfrac{27}{2}\left (e^{\ln 3}-e^{-\ln 3}\right )=\dfrac{27}{2}\left (3-\dfrac{1}{3}\right )=\dfrac{27}{2}\cdot \dfrac{8}{3} \\ =36 \end{array}$

text: If the area of the region $\left \{(x,y):\left |4-x^{2}\right |\leq y\leq x^{2},y\leq 4,x\geq 0\right \}$ is $\left (\frac{80\sqrt{2}}{α}-β\right ),α,β\in 𝐍$, then $α+β$ is equal to $_________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 2nd April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
For $x\geq 0$, the condition $|4-x^{2}|\leq x^{2}$ needs $4-x^{2}\leq x^{2}$, i.e. $x\geq \sqrt{2}$; the condition $|4-x^{2}|\leq y\leq 4$ needs $x^{2}-4\leq 4$, i.e. $x\leq 2\sqrt{2}$.

For $\sqrt{2}\leq x\leq 2$, $x^{2}\leq 4$, so $y$ runs from $4-x^{2}$ to $x^{2}$. For $2\leq x\leq 2\sqrt{2}$, $x^{2}\geq 4$, so $y$ runs from $x^{2}-4$ to $4$.


[IMG]

$\int\limits _{\sqrt{2}}^{2}\left (2x^{2}-4\right )dx=\left [\dfrac{2x^{3}}{3}-4x\right ]_{\sqrt{2}}^{2}=-\dfrac{8}{3}+\dfrac{8\sqrt{2}}{3}$

$\int\limits _{2}^{2\sqrt{2}}\left (8-x^{2}\right )dx=\left [8x-\dfrac{x^{3}}{3}\right ]_{2}^{2\sqrt{2}}=\dfrac{32\sqrt{2}}{3}-\dfrac{40}{3}$

$\text{Area}=\dfrac{40\sqrt{2}}{3}-16=\dfrac{80\sqrt{2}}{6}-16$

Comparing with $\dfrac{80\sqrt{2}}{α}-β$ gives $α=6$, $β=16$, so $α+β=22$.

Hence, the answer is 22.

text: Let [.] denote the greatest integer function. If $\int\limits _{0}^{e^{3}}\left [\frac{1}{e^{x-1}}\right ]dx=α-\log _{e}2$, then $α^{3}$ is equal to $_________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 2nd April Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
To solve this, we start by evaluating the integral:

$I=\int\limits _{0}^{e^{3}}\left [\frac{1}{e^{x-1}}\right ]dx$

The greatest integer function $[\cdot ]$ returns the largest integer less than or equal to the input value. Here's how we can approach the problem:

Determine the function inside the integral:  

$\frac{1}{e^{x-1}}=e^{1-x}$.

Identifying the intervals:

When $e^{1-x}\geq 2$, which simplifies to $x\leq 1-\ln 2$, we have $\left [e^{1-x}\right ]=2$.

When $1\leq e^{1-x}<2$, simplifying gives $1-\ln 2<x\leq 1$, and thus $\left [e^{1-x}\right ]=1$.

When $0\leq e^{1-x}<1$, which holds for $x>1$, thus $\left [e^{1-x}\right ]=0$ from $x=1$ to $x=e^{3}$.

Evaluate the integral on these intervals:

$\int\limits _{0}^{1-\ln 2}2dx=2(1-\ln 2)$ 

$\int\limits _{1-\ln 2}^{1}1dx=1-(1-\ln 2)=\ln 2$ 

$\int\limits _{1}^{e^{3}}0\qquad dx=0$

Combine these results:

$I=2(1-\ln 2)+\ln 2+0=2-\ln 2$

Thus, we are given that:

$α-\ln 2=2-\ln 2$

This implies that:

$α=2$

Therefore, $α^{3}=2^{3}=8$.
